# The US and Iran have agreed a ceasefire, with talks to bridge the gulf between them. Here’s what to know

By

Jessie Yeung

PUBLISHED

Iranians took to the streets after the ceasefire announcement at Enqelab Square, Tehran, on April 8, 2026.

Stringer/AFP/Getty Images

See all topics

Email 

Link Copied!

After a month and a half of spiraling conflict in the Middle East, the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire on Tuesday – less than two hours before US President Donald Trump’s deadline, after which he had promised to wipe out a “whole civilization.” [...] That threat, which critics warned could be a war crime if carried out, appears to have been staved off for now at the 11th hour. But there remains a gulf between the two countries, who each portrayed the temporary truce as a victory for their nations.

The ceasefire is a starting point for further negotiations, and it remains to be seen what final terms may be included in a proposal to definitively end a war that has upended the Middle East and caused a historic global oil disruption.

Here’s what we know.

## What have the US and Israel said?

US President Donald Trump spoke about the war with Iran in the White House on April 6, 2026.

Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images [...] Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

Trump announced the ceasefire in a Truth Social post, saying it was made on the condition that Iran agree to reopen the critical Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s oil flows.

The ceasefire had been mediated by Pakistan’s prime minister and its military chief, he said. Iran had put forth a 10-point proposal, which the US views as “a workable basis on which to negotiate,” Trump added.

The next two weeks will allow a final agreement to be drawn up, he said.

Crowds of Iranians took to the streets of Tehran Wednesday to celebrate a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, with footage showing demonstrators burning U.S. and Israeli flags while chanting anti-American slogans.

Demonstrators gathered at Enqelab-e-Eslami (Islamic Revolution) Square, clutching Iranian flags and posters of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.
